newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan's current account surplus keeps falling.
newsitem.headline: Japan's current account surplus keeps falling.

text.p: Japan's huge current account surplus -- the broadest measure of trade in goods and services -- plunged 35.3 percent in the six months to September compared with a year ago, confirming that the declining trend is still in place despite the weaker yen, official data showed on Monday.
The current account surplus for the first half of the fiscal year, which started in April, stood at 3.33 trillion yen, according to the Ministry of Finance.

At Monday's exchange rate of around 112 yen to the dollar, the first-half current account surplus was equivalent to $29.7 billion. The surplus in merchandise trade alone in the six months decreased by 32.1 percent to 4.155 trillion yen ($37 billion) from the same period a year earlier.

The ministry also released figures for the September current account surplus, which fell 35.6 percent from a year earlier to 727.4 billion yen ($6.49 billion). The merchandise trade surplus for September slid 27.1 percent to 973.7 billion yen ($8.69 billion).
Economists had expected the September current account surplus to have fallen to an average 860.7 billion yen ($7.68 billion) in September from 1.13 trillion yen ($10.0 billion) a year earlier.

They said the pace of the decline in the surplus has been slowing recently mainly due to the the yen's weakness against the dollar, which has fuelled a rebound in exports and capped growth in imports.
